title: Faithfulness in Small Things — Luke 16:10
paragraphs: The test of your calling is usually hidden in what feels too small to matter.

A quiet task.
A private choice.
A moment nobody claps for.
Jesus said, “One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much” (Luke 16:10).

That means the real battle is not only in the big decisions.
It is in the little ones.
How you speak when irritated.
How you handle money when no one checks.
How you pray when nobody sees.
How you obey when the reward is delayed.
We want platforms. God watches patterns.

And that’s where conviction hits.
Some of us are asking for more while neglecting what is already in our hands.
We want greater influence, greater favor, greater open doors.
But Heaven pays attention to the unseen stewardship before the public assignment.

But here’s what we miss: this is not about earning God’s love.
This is about revealing whether our hearts are surrendered.
Faithfulness in small things does not save us. Jesus does.
Yet the saved life begins to show itself in everyday obedience, honest repentance, and steady trust.

When you fail in the little things, don’t run from Christ.
Run to Him.
His blood covers the careless moment, the compromised choice, the half-hearted season.
And His grace does more than forgive. It retrains the heart.

So be faithful with the little.
The hidden place.
The hard place.
The ordinary place.
Because in the Kingdom, small obedience is never small.
